$comment: Scripted days for James. See scenarios/sarah.json for the field semantics. Day 1 is the reason this persona exists.

days.label: An ordinary day — a TRUE calm state, only the always-on dosha rule fired
No wrist temperature since Monday — RHR 26% up, rule 1.3 can't be checked, Partial
days.$note: The design pack's James (B2 Partial). Rule 1.3 is dual-gated on temperature AND RHR. RHR is up, temperature is missing, so 1.3 is UNEVALUABLE and the app says so instead of reassuring him. Until plan v2 §3 this persona carried a present, normal temperature and this day read 'in balance'. That defect is still real for anyone whose temperature does come through: see day 7.

days.label: Full moon — sodium dialled down, training untouched
A real intervention — HRV well below baseline, the run is substituted
days.$note: Contrast with day 7. Same persona, same collapsed steps, same elevated RHR — the only difference is that a rule can SEE it. That contrast is the argument for rule 1.4.

days.label: HRV did not sync — partial, not falsely reassuring
days.$note: Note what this day is NOT: James has no cycle data, so rules 2.1-2.4 are unevaluable on EVERY day including day 0. If 'partial' counted those, he would be permanently partial and in_balance would be unreachable — taking F2 and F19 out of the demo entirely. That is why the predicate is narrowed to Layer 1.

days.label: THE JAMES GAP — temperature back and normal, RHR still 26% up, app says 'in balance today'
days.$note: WRONG BUT CURRENT, and shown in the harness on purpose. With a normal temperature reading, 1.3's dual gate evaluates cleanly to FALSE: no warnings, no unevaluable Layer 1 row, nothing in the Decision to tell this apart from day 0. Candidate rule 1.4 would close it (plan v2 §9.3).
